heading: DENTAL NEWS IN KATY

blocks.text: Home - DENTAL DICTIONARY
DENTAL DICTIONARY
Dentist Katy, TX
This is designed to provide some basic information regarding terms you may hear during your dental visit. For additional information on any of these topics, talk with your dental team.
blocks.html: This is designed to provide some basic information regarding terms you may hear during your dental visit. For additional information on any of these topics, talk with your dental team.

blocks.text: A

abscess – severe and/or chronic localized inflammation in the gum tissue or at the tooth root that usually presents with infection, swelling, pain, and pus, and can cause damage to surrounding teeth and bone if left untreated
blocks.html: abscess – severe and/or chronic localized inflammation in the gum tissue or at the tooth root that usually presents with infection, swelling, pain, and pus, and can cause damage to surrounding teeth and bone if left untreated

blocks.text: abutment – a natural tooth or dental implant that is used to support a fixed or removable dental prosthesis
blocks.html: abutment – a natural tooth or dental implant that is used to support a fixed or removable dental prosthesis

blocks.text: acid etching – preparation of tooth enamel or dentin surface by the use of an acidic chemical to ensure successful bonding
blocks.html: acid etching – preparation of tooth enamel or dentin surface by the use of an acidic chemical to ensure successful bonding

blocks.text: acrylic resin – compound that may be used to fabricate dental prosthetics, such as denture teeth and crowns
blocks.html: acrylic resin – compound that may be used to fabricate dental prosthetics, such as denture teeth and crowns

blocks.text: ADA – American Dental Association, an organization of professional dentists within the United States, commonly known for providing public dental health education
blocks.html: ADA – American Dental Association, an organization of professional dentists within the United States, commonly known for providing public dental health education

blocks.text: adhesion – part of the bonding process, characterized by chemical or physical agents connecting two or more surfaces with or without the use of adhesive
blocks.html: adhesion – part of the bonding process, characterized by chemical or physical agents connecting two or more surfaces with or without the use of adhesive

blocks.text: adhesive – any substance that causes two or more surfaces to maintain connection with one another for an indefinite period of time
blocks.html: adhesive – any substance that causes two or more surfaces to maintain connection with one another for an indefinite period of time

blocks.text: air abrasion – the use of a tool that blasts air and abrasive material at a tooth to remove small amounts of tooth structure
blocks.html: air abrasion – the use of a tool that blasts air and abrasive material at a tooth to remove small amounts of tooth structure

blocks.text: alloy/amalgam – compound made up of two or more elements and containing properties not found in the individual elements
blocks.html: alloy/amalgam – compound made up of two or more elements and containing properties not found in the individual elements

blocks.text: alveolar – part of the jaw bone where teeth are anchored
blocks.html: alveolar – part of the jaw bone where teeth are anchored

blocks.text: anesthesia (local) – medication used to block pain in one area for treatment
blocks.html: anesthesia (local) – medication used to block pain in one area for treatment

blocks.text: anesthesia (general) – medication used to induce partial or complete unconsciousness during treatment
blocks.html: anesthesia (general) – medication used to induce partial or complete unconsciousness during treatment

blocks.text: anterior – refers to teeth or tissues in the front part of the mouth
blocks.html: anterior – refers to teeth or tissues in the front part of the mouth

blocks.text: ANUG – Acute Necrotizing Ulcerative Gingivitis, a condition characterized by small ulcers in the gums and aggravated by stress or smoking
blocks.html: ANUG – Acute Necrotizing Ulcerative Gingivitis, a condition characterized by small ulcers in the gums and aggravated by stress or smoking

blocks.text: apex – tip of the tooth root
blocks.html: apex – tip of the tooth root

blocks.text: apicoectomy – surgical amputation of a tooth root to treat a dead tooth
blocks.html: apicoectomy – surgical amputation of a tooth root to treat a dead tooth

blocks.text: appliance – oral device such as braces, mouth guards, or retainers
blocks.html: appliance – oral device such as braces, mouth guards, or retainers

blocks.text: arch – curved structure of upper or lower teeth
blocks.html: arch – curved structure of upper or lower teeth

blocks.text: archwire – metal wire used in braces to guide teeth into proper alignment
blocks.html: archwire – metal wire used in braces to guide teeth into proper alignment

blocks.text: arthrogram – diagnostic x-ray involving injection of contrast dye into joint to view the bone structures
blocks.html: arthrogram – diagnostic x-ray involving injection of contrast dye into joint to view the bone structures

blocks.text: artificial crown – prosthetic tooth restoration that covers or replaces a tooth, may attach to partial tooth or dental implant
blocks.html: artificial crown – prosthetic tooth restoration that covers or replaces a tooth, may attach to partial tooth or dental implant

blocks.text: attrition – natural wear causing loss of structure
blocks.html: attrition – natural wear causing loss of structure

blocks.text: augmentation – procedure that treats a deficiency of soft tissue or bone structure
blocks.html: augmentation – procedure that treats a deficiency of soft tissue or bone structure

blocks.text: avulsion/evulsion – removal of tooth from socket due to trauma
blocks.html: avulsion/evulsion – removal of tooth from socket due to trauma

blocks.text: B
band – metal ring cemented in place around a tooth to allow brackets to attach to the teeth
blocks.html: band – metal ring cemented in place around a tooth to allow brackets to attach to the teeth

blocks.text: banding – orthodontic process of fitting and cementing bands to teeth
blocks.html: banding – orthodontic process of fitting and cementing bands to teeth

blocks.text: base – insulating substance used beneath restorations to protect tooth pulp from changes in temperature
blocks.html: base – insulating substance used beneath restorations to protect tooth pulp from changes in temperature

blocks.text: benefit – payment for covered dental services by third party insurer
blocks.html: benefit – payment for covered dental services by third party insurer

blocks.text: benign – a term used to indicate mild, non-threatening, or non-malignant
blocks.html: benign – a term used to indicate mild, non-threatening, or non-malignant

blocks.text: bicuspid – tooth located in front of the molars and behind cuspids
blocks.html: bicuspid – tooth located in front of the molars and behind cuspids

blocks.text: bilateral – term meaning both right and left sides are indicated
blocks.html: bilateral – term meaning both right and left sides are indicated

blocks.text: biopsy – the removal of a small amount of tissue for examination and/or testing
blocks.html: biopsy – the removal of a small amount of tissue for examination and/or testing

blocks.text: bioinert – material property indicating it causes no physical reaction, such as inflammation or immune response
blocks.html: bioinert – material property indicating it causes no physical reaction, such as inflammation or immune response

blocks.text: bite/occlusion – physical relationship between upper and lower teeth when closed
blocks.html: bite/occlusion – physical relationship between upper and lower teeth when closed

blocks.text: bleaching – whitening of the teeth, generally using a chemical oxidizing agent and/or laser treatment
blocks.html: bleaching – whitening of the teeth, generally using a chemical oxidizing agent and/or laser treatment

blocks.text: block injection – anesthetic placed to cause numbness over a large area of the jaw and mouth
blocks.html: block injection – anesthetic placed to cause numbness over a large area of the jaw and mouth

blocks.text: block graft – bone graft stabilized with screw, generally used to correct large bone defect
blocks.html: block graft – bone graft stabilized with screw, generally used to correct large bone defect

blocks.text: bond – mechanical or chemical adhesion connecting two surfaces, orthodontic appliance seal
blocks.html: bond – mechanical or chemical adhesion connecting two surfaces, orthodontic appliance seal

blocks.text: bonding – process of attaching brackets to teeth for braces or restoring teeth with composite resin to repair tooth color or shape
blocks.html: bonding –  process of attaching brackets to teeth for braces or restoring teeth with composite resin to repair tooth color or shape

blocks.text: bone atrophy/resorption – loss of bone in jaw, commonly caused by periodontal disease
blocks.html: bone atrophy/resorption – loss of bone in jaw, commonly caused by periodontal disease

blocks.text: braces – orthodontic devices used to reposition teeth over time to correct misalignment, generally consisting of brackets and archwires
blocks.html: braces – orthodontic devices used to reposition teeth over time to correct misalignment, generally consisting of brackets and archwires

blocks.text: bracket – ceramic or metal piece cemented to the tooth to hold an archwire for orthodontic treatment
blocks.html: bracket – ceramic or metal piece cemented to the tooth to hold an archwire for orthodontic treatment

blocks.text: bridge/partial denture – dental prosthetic device used to replace one or more missing teeth, generally attaches to surrounding teeth or implants for support
blocks.html: bridge/partial denture – dental prosthetic device used to replace one or more missing teeth, generally attaches to surrounding teeth or implants for support

blocks.text: bruxism – involuntary grinding of the teeth, usually while sleeping, often causing tooth wear, sensitivity, headaches, and jaw pain
blocks.html: bruxism – involuntary grinding of the teeth, usually while sleeping, often causing tooth wear, sensitivity, headaches, and jaw pain

blocks.text: buccal – referring to or toward the cheek
blocks.html: buccal – referring to or toward the cheek

blocks.text: C
CAD/CAM – Computer -Aided Design/Computer-Aided Manufacturing
blocks.html: CAD/CAM – Computer -Aided Design/Computer-Aided Manufacturing

blocks.text: calcium – mineral necessary to the formation and maintenance of healthy teeth and bones
blocks.html: calcium – mineral necessary to the formation and maintenance of healthy teeth and bones

blocks.text: calculus – commonly called “tartar,” hard substance that forms on teeth due to insufficient plaque control, may be stained brown or yellow
blocks.html: calculus – commonly called “tartar,” hard substance that forms on teeth due to insufficient plaque control, may be stained brown or yellow

blocks.text: canker sore – whitish mouth sore, usually lasts 10-14 days, may have red “halo”
blocks.html: canker sore – whitish mouth sore, usually lasts 10-14 days, may have red “halo”

blocks.text: cantilever bridge – dental bridge that only attaches to teeth on one side
blocks.html: cantilever bridge – dental bridge that only attaches to teeth on one side

blocks.text: cap – commonly used term for dental crown
blocks.html: cap – commonly used term for dental crown

blocks.text: caries – common term for tooth decay or “cavities”
blocks.html: caries – common term for tooth decay or “cavities”

blocks.text: cast/model – 3D reproduction used by filling an impression or mold with plaster and allowing it to dry
blocks.html: cast/model – 3D reproduction used by filling an impression or mold with plaster and allowing it to dry

blocks.text: CAT scan – Computerized Axial Tomography scan, used to determine size, shape, and placement of bone, usually used for implant placement planning
blocks.html: CAT scan – Computerized Axial Tomography scan, used to determine size, shape, and placement of bone, usually used for implant placement planning

blocks.text: cavity – missing tooth structure caused by decay, abrasion, or erosion
blocks.html: cavity – missing tooth structure caused by decay, abrasion, or erosion

blocks.text: Cavitron – dental tool used in cleaning teeth, uses high-frequency ultrasonic waves
blocks.html: Cavitron – dental tool used in cleaning teeth, uses high-frequency ultrasonic waves

blocks.text: cellulitis – potentially dangerous infection of the soft tissue, characterized by extensive hard swelling
blocks.html: cellulitis – potentially dangerous infection of the soft tissue, characterized by extensive hard swelling

blocks.text: cementum – hard tissue that covers the outer surface of a tooth root
blocks.html: cementum – hard tissue that covers the outer surface of a tooth root

blocks.text: cephalometric imaging – x-ray scan of the head that shows the relative positioning of the face, teeth, and jaws
blocks.html: cephalometric imaging – x-ray scan of the head that shows the relative positioning of the face, teeth, and jaws

blocks.text: clasp – acrylic or metal portion of a partial denture that hooks to natural teeth
blocks.html: clasp – acrylic or metal portion of a partial denture that hooks to natural teeth

blocks.text: cleaning/prophylaxis – the removal of plaque and calculus from the teeth above the gumline
blocks.html: cleaning/prophylaxis – the removal of plaque and calculus from the teeth above the gumline

blocks.text: cleft palate – congenital deformity that is characterized by a partial or complete lack of fusion of soft and/or hard palate
blocks.html: cleft palate – congenital deformity that is characterized by a partial or complete lack of fusion of soft and/or hard palate

blocks.text: coil spring – spring used between brackets and archwire to open or close space between teeth
blocks.html: coil spring – spring used between brackets and archwire to open or close space between teeth

blocks.text: complete denture – set of prosthetic teeth that are used to replace all upper or lower teeth
blocks.html: complete denture – set of prosthetic teeth that are used to replace all upper or lower teeth

blocks.text: composite resin – tooth colored material composed of plastic with small particles of ceramic or glass, generally cured with a chemical catalyst or filtered light
blocks.html: composite resin – tooth colored material composed of plastic with small particles of ceramic or glass, generally cured with a chemical catalyst or filtered light

blocks.text: coronal – referencing the crown of a tooth
blocks.html: coronal – referencing the crown of a tooth

blocks.text: cosmetic dentistry – dental services used to improve appearance, rather than health or function
blocks.html: cosmetic dentistry – dental services used to improve appearance, rather than health or function

blocks.text: cross bite – lower teeth lie in front of upper teeth when teeth are closed
blocks.html: cross bite – lower teeth lie in front of upper teeth when teeth are closed

blocks.text: crown – may refer to the visible tooth above the gumline or to a prosthetic dental restoration that replaces part or all of a natural tooth
blocks.html: crown – may refer to the visible tooth above the gumline or to a prosthetic dental restoration that replaces part or all of a natural tooth

blocks.text: crown lengthening – surgical manipulation of gum tissue to expose more tooth structure, often used in conjunction with other treatment
blocks.html: crown lengthening – surgical manipulation of gum tissue to expose more tooth structure, often used in conjunction with other treatment

blocks.text: curettage – the removal of infected tissues from periodontal pocket or bone, often in conjunction with scaling and root planing (deep cleaning)
blocks.html: curettage – the removal of infected tissues from periodontal pocket or bone, often in conjunction with scaling and root planing (deep cleaning)

blocks.text: cusp – pointed or rounded mound on or near the chewing surface of a tooth
blocks.html: cusp – pointed or rounded mound on or near the chewing surface of a tooth

blocks.text: cuspid – tooth located between incisors and bicuspids, also known as “eye tooth” or “canine”
blocks.html: cuspid – tooth located between incisors and bicuspids, also known as “eye tooth” or “canine”

blocks.html: cyst – sac of tissue, usually hard or filled with fluid

blocks.text: D
DDS – Doctor of Dental Surgery, this degree is equivalent to DMD
blocks.html: DDS – Doctor of Dental Surgery, this degree is equivalent to DMD

blocks.text: debridement – removal of plaque and calculus that is interfering with proper evaluation
blocks.html: debridement – removal of plaque and calculus that is interfering with proper evaluation

blocks.text: debanding – removal of cemented orthodontic bands from teeth
blocks.html: debanding – removal of cemented orthodontic bands from teeth

blocks.text: debonding – removal of cemented orthodontic brackets from teeth
blocks.html: debonding – removal of cemented orthodontic brackets from teeth

blocks.text: decay – the destruction of tooth structure
blocks.html: decay – the destruction of tooth structure

blocks.text: deciduous teeth – also known as “baby” or “primary” teeth, these first teeth generally arrive between the ages of birth and 3 and will fall out later as permanent teeth begin to erupt in their place
blocks.html: deciduous teeth – also known as “baby” or “primary” teeth, these first teeth generally arrive between the ages of birth and 3 and will fall out later as permanent teeth begin to erupt in their place

blocks.text: dental implant – small cylinder, generally titanium, implanted into the upper or lower jawbone to anchor a dental appliance or restoration
blocks.html: dental implant – small cylinder, generally titanium, implanted into the upper or lower jawbone to anchor a dental appliance or restoration

blocks.text: dentin – hard inner layer of the tooth, just beneath the enamel, forms the bulk of the tooth structure
blocks.html: dentin – hard inner layer of the tooth, just beneath the enamel, forms the bulk of the tooth structure

blocks.text: dentistry – medical field characterized by the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases and disorders of the teeth, mouth, gums, jaws, and other oral and maxillofacial areas by a trained and certified professional
blocks.html: dentistry – medical field characterized by the evaluation, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of diseases and disorders of the teeth, mouth, gums, jaws, and other oral and maxillofacial areas by a trained and certified professional

blocks.text: dentition – the arrangement of teeth within the mouth
blocks.html: dentition – the arrangement of teeth within the mouth

blocks.text: denture – set of one or more prosthetic teeth
blocks.html: denture – set of one or more prosthetic teeth

blocks.text: diagnostic cast – impression used to aid in planning treatment
blocks.html: diagnostic cast – impression used to aid in planning treatment

blocks.text: diagnostic imaging – photographs or radiographs taken for the purpose of diagnostic evaluation
blocks.html: diagnostic imaging – photographs or radiographs taken for the purpose of diagnostic evaluation

blocks.text: diastema – the space between two adjacent teeth
blocks.html: diastema – the space between two adjacent teeth

blocks.text: discectomy – removal of intra-articular disc from a joint
blocks.html: discectomy – removal of intra-articular disc from a joint

blocks.html: displaced tooth – tooth that has grown or shifted into an incorrect placement within the mouth

blocks.text: distal – part of the tooth furthest from the center of the arch
blocks.html: distal – part of the tooth furthest from the center of the arch

blocks.text: DMD – Doctor of Medical Dentistry, this degree is equivalent to DDS
blocks.html: DMD – Doctor of Medical Dentistry, this degree is equivalent to DDS

blocks.text: dressing – medicines, bandages, or other materials applied to a wound to promote healing
blocks.html: dressing – medicines, bandages, or other materials applied to a wound to promote healing

blocks.text: dry socket – painful localized inflammation of a tooth socket after extraction, caused by infection or loss of the blood clot needed for proper healing
blocks.html: dry socket – painful localized inflammation of a tooth socket after extraction, caused by infection or loss of the blood clot needed for proper healing

edentulous – term meaning “without teeth”
blocks.html: edentulous – term meaning “without teeth”

blocks.text: enamel – hard tissue exterior of a tooth, covers the dentin
blocks.html: enamel – hard tissue exterior of a tooth, covers the dentin

blocks.text: endodontics – dental field concerned with care and treatment of tooth pulp and associated areas
blocks.html: endodontics – dental field concerned with care and treatment of tooth pulp and associated areas

blocks.html: endodontist – dental specialist focused on treating disease and injuries of the tooth pulp and associated areas

blocks.html: epidemiology – scientific study of disease incidence and prevalence in a population

blocks.text: equilibration – reshaping bite surfaces of teeth to correct imbalance, also known as occlusal adjustment
blocks.html: equilibration – reshaping bite surfaces of teeth to correct imbalance, also known as occlusal adjustment

blocks.text: eruption – protrusion of teeth through gums
blocks.html: eruption – protrusion of teeth through gums

blocks.text: evulsion/avulsion – removal of tooth from socket due to trauma
blocks.html: evulsion/avulsion – removal of tooth from socket due to trauma

blocks.text: excision – removal of tissue or bone through surgical means
blocks.html: excision – removal of tissue or bone through surgical means

blocks.text: exodontia – dental extraction
blocks.html: exodontia – dental extraction

blocks.text: exostosis – bone overgrowth
blocks.html: exostosis – bone overgrowth

blocks.text: extraoral – refers to the area outside the oral cavity
blocks.html: extraoral – refers to the area outside the oral cavity

blocks.text: extracoronal – refers to the area outside the crown of a tooth

blocks.text: extraction – removal of a tooth
blocks.html: extraction – removal of a tooth

blocks.text: exudate – material containing fluid, cells, and/or debris caused by necrosis or inflammation
blocks.html: exudate – material containing fluid, cells, and/or debris caused by necrosis or inflammation

blocks.text: eyeteeth – common term for cuspid or “canine” teeth
blocks.html: eyeteeth – common term for cuspid or “canine” teeth

general anesthesia – the use of medication to induce a controlled unconscious state in a patient during treatment, allows reduced or eliminated sensation of pain and reflexive motion
blocks.html: general anesthesia – the use of medication to induce a controlled unconscious state in a patient during treatment, allows reduced or eliminated sensation of pain and reflexive motion

blocks.html: gingiva – also called gum tissue, soft tissue that surrounds teeth within the mouth

blocks.html: gingivectomy – surgical removal of gum tissue/gingiva

blocks.html: gingivitis – stage of periodontal disease where gum tissue is inflamed and/or infected, but loss of tissues has not occurred

blocks.html: graft – surgical addition of natural or synthetic tissue to repair or reinforce tissues with defect or deficiency

blocks.html: Guided Tissue Regeneration (GTR) – advanced surgical technique used to enhance bone regeneration/regrowth

blocks.html: gum recession – shrinkage of gums due to periodontal disease, surgery, or other cause resulting in exposure of teeth roots

halitosis – chronic bad breath, generally caused by oral or gastrointestinal disorder

blocks.html: hematoma – blood swelling beneath the surface of the skin, gums, or other tissue

blocks.html: hygienist – dental professional who is trained and certified to perform dental cleanings, scaling and root planing, and other functions, provides patient education, and may administer local anesthetic or nitrous oxide

blocks.html: hyperplasia – abnormal increase in cell growth leading to enlargement of tissue

imaging – includes, but is not limited to, X-rays, CAT scans, MRIs, photographs, and other visual diagnostic formats
blocks.html: imaging – includes, but is not limited to, X-rays, CAT scans, MRIs, photographs, and other visual diagnostic formats

blocks.html: immediate denture – teeth replacement prosthetic designed to be placed as soon as teeth are removed, generally will be replaced with permanent denture once healing is complete

blocks.html: immediate implant placement – dental implant placed during the same visit as the extraction of the tooth it replaces

blocks.html: impacted tooth – a tooth that is partially or fully unable to erupt and remains embedded in soft tissue or wedged against bone or another tooth

blocks.text: implant – to insert or graft material into tissue
blocks.html: implant – to insert or graft material into tissue

blocks.text: implant, dental – small metal cylinder, usually titanium, placed in or on jawbone, used in conjunction with dental prosthetic as a tooth replacement solution
blocks.html: implant, dental – small metal cylinder, usually titanium, placed in or on jawbone, used in conjunction with dental prosthetic as a tooth replacement solution

blocks.html: implant dentistry – field of study and practice involving the surgical placement and maintenance of dental implants and implant-anchored tooth replacement prosthetics

blocks.html: impression – mold of teeth and gums, made by biting a soft material, used for diagnostic and treatment planning purposes

blocks.html: incision and drainage – small surgical cut to drain pus from an abscess

blocks.text: inlay – filling made outside the tooth, then cemented or bonded in place to restore lost structure

blocks.text: interproximal – adjacent surfaces between teeth within the same arch

blocks.text: interocclusal – between upper and lower teeth of the bite
blocks.html: interocclusal – between upper and lower teeth of the bite

blocks.text: intracoronal – inside the tooth crown
blocks.html: intracoronal – inside the tooth crown

blocks.text: intraoral – inside the oral cavity
blocks.html: intraoral – inside the oral cavity

blocks.text: intraoral camera – specially designed camera for use in photographing inside the mouth, used for diagnostic purposes
blocks.html: intraoral camera – specially designed camera for use in photographing inside the mouth, used for diagnostic purposes

jacket crown – prosthetic crown for a front tooth

blocks.text: jaw – common term referring to maxilla or mandible bone
blocks.html: jaw – common term referring to maxilla or mandible bone

blocks.html: local anesthesia – medication used to block nerve impulses to provide partial or complete elimination of pain during treatment

blocks.html: malocclusion – improper alignment of upper and lower jaw or teeth

blocks.text: mandible – lower jaw

blocks.html: maxillary sinus – open cavity inside the maxilla

blocks.html: night guard – appliance used to protect teeth and jaw during sleep in cases of grinding

blocks.text: nitrous oxide – also known as laughing gas, odorless inhalant that causes a mild sedative effect
blocks.html: nitrous oxide – also known as laughing gas, odorless inhalant that causes a mild sedative effect
